We are narrowing our full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook, while maintaining the midpoint of the prior range, supported by solid year-to-date performance and increased visibility into expected results for the remainder of the year.

Our outlook includes a full year of operating results from the Advanced Polymer Technologies reportable segment and excludes contributions from the divested industrial specialties product line, effective January 1, 2026, and the road markings product line beginning April 15, 2026.

We expect Net sales in our Performance Materials reportable segment to grow low-single digits as increased pricing on certain products partially offsets the forecasted decline in global automotive production for Internal Combustion Engine ("ICE") powertrains compared to the prior year.

We expect Net sales in our Pavement Technologies reportable segment, excluding the divested road markings product line beginning April 15, 2026, to grow low-single digits, reflecting demand softness from higher asphalt costs.

For our Advanced Polymer Technologies reportable segment, we expect Net sales to grow low-double digits with low-single digit volume growth, reflecting the benefit of price surcharges implemented in the second and third quarters of 2026 in response to higher raw materials costs.

We expect our Performance Materials reportable segment to maintain segment EBITDA margins around mid-50 percent, as revenue growth is partially offset by investments in selective growth opportunities.

In our Pavement Technologies reportable segment, we expect segment EBITDA margins in the mid-teens, reflecting higher input and logistics costs and the burden of dis-synergy from the divested road markings product line.
We anticipate that our Advanced Polymer Technologies reportable segment EBITDA will improve versus prior year driven by volume growth, while maintaining segment EBITDA margins of around 20 percent.
We expect to achieve run rate savings of approximately 75% of these costs by the end of 2026.
Our effective tax rate is expected to be between 22 and 24 percent.

We expect to recognize between $80 million and $90 million of depreciation and amortization, reflecting the divested road markings product line and asset impairments recognized in the second quarter of 2026.
Additionally, discrete tax items could drive variability in our projected effective tax rate.

Over the next twelve months, we expect to fund the following: debt principal repayments, interest payments, capital expenditures, income tax payments, purchases pursuant to our stock repurchase program (and related excise tax payments), and restructuring activities.

In connection with such transactions, or to fund other anticipated uses of cash, we may modify our existing revolving credit facility, redeem all or part of our outstanding senior notes, seek additional debt financing, issue equity securities, or some combination thereof.
We believe that our foreign holdings of cash will not have a material adverse impact on our U.S. liquidity.

Shares under the 2022 Authorization may be purchased through open market or privately negotiated transactions at the discretion of management based on its evaluation of prevailing market conditions and other factors, including through the use of trading plans intended to qualify under Rule 10b5-1 under the Exchange Act.
We have no material commitments associated with these projected capital expenditures as of September 30, 2026 .

The company expects full-year net sales of approximately $1.1 billion and diluted adjusted EPS of $5.25 to $5.45.
